punchline: At Spartak in Moscow, a world top-ten player and a five-year-old start the same way: bouncing and catching a ball.
thirty_sec: Daniel Coyle visited a rundown Moscow tennis club with one indoor court, which he reports produced more top-20 women than the whole United States in recent years. What struck him was the practice. Everyone, from five-year-olds to a top-ten player, starts with the same ball-handling warm-up, then swings in slow motion, and sometimes with no ball at all. Players don't compete until they've practiced for three years. One coach told him technique is everything.
